The mirror types `add.picker.filter` as **`unknown`** while the component that consumes it types the same thing as **`ViewFilterRule[]`**, and four `(schema as any).add` reads keep the divergence invisible.

Seat-verified at source on `origin/main` `8f37c4e90`, `packages/types/src/record-components.ts:399`:

```ts
    picker: { object: string; valueField?: string; labelField?: string; filter?: unknown };
```

⇒ the authoring face declares 「anything」 for a key the renderer's own component declares as a typed rule array. Measured by the objectui#9475 dev (relayed and attributed): **un-casting all four `(schema as any).add` reads in `record-related-list.tsx` yields exactly one `TS2322`** — the divergence, surfacing the moment the casts stop hiding it.

## ⭐ Why the looser side is the wrong side here

`RelatedList`'s own comment records that the tighter type was **deliberate** — objectui#3831: 「a looser type here is where a wrong shape would hide」. ⇒ the intent exists and is written down; what it does ⛔ not do is **reach the authoring face**, which is the one an author (or an AI writing metadata) reads.

## ⚠️ Why it is filed and ⛔ not fixed

Repairing it means moving one of the two declarations:
- `packages/types/src/record-components.ts` is **fenced** — PR objectui#9895 holds 100 files under `packages/types`;
- `RelatedList.tsx` was outside objectui#9475's declared surface.

⇒ neither side was this card's dev to move, and it ledgered the divergence live in its new pin instead of leaving it as prose.

## ⛔ What this card does NOT settle

Which declaration moves. Tightening the mirror to `ViewFilterRule[]` narrows a **published authoring surface**; loosening the component throws away a guard objectui#3831 put there on purpose. ⚠️ That is a contract question for whoever takes it, ⛔ not a cleanup.
